records.gloss: For the director, with stringed instruments. A psalm. A song.
pieces: For the music director. With stringed instruments. A psalm. A song.

L.1: For the director: with stringed instruments. A psalm; a song.

R.1: For the leader of the music. To be played on stringed instruments. A song.

decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director: the one who leads the music
decisions.reason: As in 4:1, probably the leader of the temple music.

decisions.choice: stringed instruments: to be accompanied by strings
decisions.reason: As in 4:1 and 54:1, the word (neginot) means music played on stringed instruments.
Readable gives one plain word for the two words for a song.

records.heading: May all the peoples praise you, God

records.source: אֱלֹהִ֗ים יְחָנֵּ֥נוּ וִֽיבָרְכֵ֑נוּ יָ֤אֵ֥ר פָּנָ֖יו אִתָּ֣נוּ סֶֽלָה׃
records.gloss: God, may he be gracious to us and bless us; may he make shine his face with us. Selah.
pieces: May God show us grace and bless us; \q may {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} let the light of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face shine on us. Selah

L.2: God, may {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} be gracious to us and bless us; \q may {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} make {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face shine among us. Selah

R.2: May God be kind to us and bless us. \q May {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} look on us with a smile of favor. Selah

decisions.reason: The words echo the blessing the priests spoke over Israel: "The LORD bless you and keep you; the LORD make his face shine on you and be gracious to you" (Numbers 6:24-26). Here the people ask it for themselves, so that the nations may come to know God (verse 3).

decisions.choice: God in place of the name
decisions.reason: The priestly blessing uses the name, the LORD; this psalm says "God". Psalms 42-83 mostly call God "God" ('elohim) where other psalms use the name (compare Psalm 53 with Psalm 14). The word in the text is rendered.

decisions.choice: make his face shine: look on with favor
decisions.reason: A shining face is a kind and favorable look, as of a king pleased with a subject (4:7; 31:17; Proverbs 16:15).

decisions.choice: look on us with a smile of favor
alternatives: make his face shine on us
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (m3).

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.
Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

records.gloss: To know on the earth your way, among all nations your salvation.
pieces: Then the earth will know {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ways, \q and every nation {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} power to save.

L.3: That [they may] know on the earth {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} way, \q among all nations {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} salvation.

R.3: Then everyone on earth will learn what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are like. \q All nations will see how {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} save.

decisions.choice: to know: the purpose of the blessing
decisions.reason: The verb is an infinitive, "to know", that depends on verse 2: God's blessing on Israel is meant to make him known to all nations (Genesis 12:2-3). The Selah between them does not break the thought.

decisions.choice: your way: how God acts and what he requires
decisions.reason: God's way is both his way of dealing with people and the way he teaches them to live (25:4; 103:7).
The word (yeshu'ah) is God's rescue of his people from danger.
Balanced and Readable begin a new sentence after the Selah and state the purpose as a result.

records.gloss: Peoples will praise you, God; peoples will praise you, all of them.
pieces: May the peoples give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} thanks, God; \q may every people give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} thanks!

L.4: Peoples will praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, God; \q peoples will praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, all of them.

R.4: God, may people of every nation praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}! \q May all of them praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!

decisions.reason: The verbs can be read as a wish ("may they praise") or a statement of what will happen. As in verse 2, the psalm is a prayer, so Balanced and Readable say "may".
The verb (yadah) is to praise by declaring what someone has done; it includes thanks and confession.
This verse is repeated as verse 6. The two refrains frame the center of the psalm, verse 5.

records.source: יִֽשְׂמְח֥וּ וִֽירַנְּנ֗וּ לְאֻ֫מִּ֥ים כִּֽי־תִשְׁפֹּ֣ט עַמִּ֣ים מִישׁ֑וֹר וּלְאֻמִּ֓ים׀בָּאָ֖רֶץ תַּנְחֵ֣ם סֶֽלָה׃
records.gloss: Nations will rejoice and sing for joy, for you judge peoples [with] uprightness, and nations on the earth you guide them. Selah.
pieces: Let the nations celebrate and shout with joy, \q because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} judge the peoples fairly \q and lead the nations across the earth. Selah

L.5: Nations will rejoice and sing for joy, \q for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} judge peoples [with] uprightness, \q and nations on the earth, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} guide them. Selah

R.5: May the nations be happy and sing! \q You judge people in a way that is fair, \q and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} lead the nations of the world. Selah

decisions.reason: To judge (shafat) is to govern and to set things right; the nations rejoice because God's rule is fair to them (96:10-13).

decisions.choice: uprightness: what is level and fair
decisions.reason: The word (mishor) is level ground, and so fairness.
The verb (nachah) is used of leading a flock or leading Israel in the wilderness (23:3; 77:21).

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.
Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

records.gloss: Peoples will praise you, God; peoples will praise you, all of them.
pieces: May the peoples give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} thanks, God; \q may every people give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} thanks!

L.6: Peoples will praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, God; \q peoples will praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, all of them.

R.6: God, may people of every nation praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}! \q May all of them praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!

decisions.reason: The refrain of verse 4 returns word for word.

records.source: אֶ֭רֶץ נָתְנָ֣ה יְבוּלָ֑הּ יְ֝בָרְכֵ֗נוּ אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: [The] earth has given its produce; he will bless us, God, our God.
pieces: The earth has brought forth its crops; \q God, our own God, will bless us.

L.7: [The] earth has given its produce; \q God, our God, will bless us.

R.7: The ground has produced its crops. \q God, our God, will keep doing us good.

decisions.choice: has given ... will bless: a harvest as a sign
alternatives: the earth will give its produce
decisions.reason: The first verb is past: a harvest has come in, perhaps the occasion of the psalm, at a harvest festival. The second can be future or a wish. The harvest is taken as a sign of the blessing still to come.
The words echo the promise of Leviticus 26:4: if Israel keeps the covenant, "the land will give its produce".
Readable says what God's blessing brings here.

records.gloss: He will bless us, God, and they will fear him, all [the] ends of [the] earth.
pieces: God is going to bless us, \q and all the far corners of the earth will hold {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in awe.

L.8: God will bless us, \q and all the ends of the earth will fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.8: God will bless us. \q Then people everywhere, even in the farthest places, will honor {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with awe.

decisions.choice: and they will fear him: the result of the blessing
alternatives: let all the ends of the earth fear him
decisions.reason: The "and" introduces the result: the nations see God's goodness to Israel and come to revere him. It may also be a wish.

decisions.choice: the ends of the earth: the farthest peoples
decisions.reason: As in 2:8 and 22:28, the phrase means all peoples, to the edges of the known world.

decisions.choice: people everywhere, even in the farthest places
decisions.reason: Readable says who is meant (m2).
